A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TokUR, with the same title, authors, and underlying research framework. Text extraction and visual inspection covered all 27 pages of v2 and 33 pages of v4, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments, including error detection, question-difficulty analysis, offline and online test-time scaling, ablations, and case studies in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and reports additional logical-reasoning, code-generation, factuality, Qwen-model, and ablation outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: v2 Equation 9 averages token uncertainties; v4 Equation 13 uses their cumulative sum for response uncertainty and main detection experiments. Length normalization remains in test-time scaling. This changes an aggregation component, while low-rank perturbation, TU/AU/EU calculations, mean-weight decoding, and particle filtering remain essentially unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 retains GSM8K, MATH500, DeepScaleR, and the math-orz difficulty study, while adding five evaluated tasks: Zebra Puzzles, Leg Counting, Color-Cube Rotation, HumanEval code generation, and FactScore factuality. Tables 2–3 therefore substantially extend actual evaluation beyond mathematical reasoning.

E2.justification: Self-Certainty and DeepConf, merely cited in v2, become evaluated comparators in mathematical error detection and offline scaling. v4 also adds UEcc and UDeg to mathematical detection comparisons, plus Negative Length and unnormalized baseline variants in Table 9. The earlier detection comparators remain, substantially strengthening the comparison set.

E3.justification: The stated posterior-sampling budget changes from M=5 to M=2, and the GSM8K dataset table changes from 7,470 to 1,300 samples, both labeled training split. v4 adds Qwen-2.5-3B/7B evaluations and Llama-3.1-8B offline scaling. FactScore introduces GPT-5-mini annotation/judging and Top-50% Precision. The perturbation sweep is now described as using GSM8K test data instead of full MATH500. These establish reported setting changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds a length-normalization ablation with a sequence-length-only control (Table 9) and a stepwise-versus-joint posterior-sampling ablation (Figure 6). Perturbation-strength and temperature analyses are revised. Conversely, v2's accuracy-versus-selection-threshold analysis and Figures 6–7 disappear. The uncertainty-distribution visualization and four reasoning case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Three-seed mean/standard-deviation reporting for detection and online scaling remains. Offline scaling retains ten repetitions and numerical uncertainty estimates, but v4 drops v2 Appendix E.2's explicit identification of these estimates as standard errors and the stated N=512 exception. This reduces reporting specificity; it does not establish an increase in independent runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds unnormalized detection results, Qwen and non-mathematical outcomes, and new ablation findings. For Llama-3.2-1B on MATH500, raw-sum TokUR(TU) reports 80.64% AUROC, while v2's normalized 57.14% is retained in Table 9; these are different scoring settings. Offline values also change: MATH500 TokUR(EU), Maj@N, N=16 changes from 30.02% to 28.28% under revised reported settings. Online results remain identical in v2 Table 2 and v4 Table 8.

T1.justification: The formal response-uncertainty definition changes from an average to a sum, and Proposition 3.1 and its Appendix C proof remove the corresponding 1/T factor from the unbiasedness statement. This is a limited mathematical revision. Assumption 3.1 restates v2's existing stepwise-sampling footnote; the chain-rule and weight-posterior derivations are otherwise substantially retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same training-free token-uncertainty framework, epistemic-confidence claim, and three reasoning applications: error detection, solution selection, and generation guidance. Although v4 removes the standalone conclusion, its substantive contribution claims remain in the introduction. The additional evaluations do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v4 introduces a consequential interpretation that sequence length provides a favorable detection bias and that normalization effects depend on the scoring method (Appendix E.5.3). It also interprets the posterior-sampling ablation as supporting stepwise sampling, adds a temperature-robustness interpretation, and attributes the highest-difficulty AUROC rebound to data imbalance. The existing computational, semantic-aggregation, and high-variance limitations are retained and moved into the main text.

D1.justification: v4 adds a source-code repository link, explicit task-dependent normalization instructions in Appendix D.1, descriptions of newly evaluated baselines, and the FactScore evaluator identity. The rank, perturbation strength, vLLM integration, mathematical prompt, and answer-parsing documentation are largely retained or relocated. The PDFs provide the code-access pointer but do not establish its contents or functionality.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion of Kirchhof et al., Devic et al., and Zhou et al., together with references for the new tasks and Qwen models. It expands the positioning against already-cited Self-Certainty and DeepConf, while removing CER and several motivation references. The central positioning as extending Bayesian uncertainty estimation to long-form reasoning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 reorganizes the query-, token-, and response-level exposition in Sections 2–3 and substantially revises experimental and related-work prose. Online scaling moves to the appendix, limitations move into the main text, and the standalone conclusion is removed. The appendices are reorganized around a new LLM-usage disclosure and revised implementation and experiment subsections.

P2.justification: v4 adds non-mathematical, Qwen, and normalization tables, expands scaling tables, and introduces a nine-panel posterior-sampling figure. Table 1 gains an internal-signal indicator and CoT reference rows; Figures 1, 4, and 5 are redrawn. The old threshold plots disappear, while Figure 2 and the online-results table move to the appendix. Case-study graphics are retained and renumbered, and the document adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's narrower evaluation, v4 provides broader task/model evidence, evaluated contemporary baselines, and useful controls for length bias and posterior sampling. Table 9 particularly improves understanding of what drives detection performance. These benefits are partly offset by reporting problems: Figure 2 retains the earlier scaling results despite revised Table 7 values, offline uncertainty reporting becomes less explicit, and blanket outperformance statements overlook exceptions in Table 1. The net quality improvement is positive but qualified.
